statement: Every predicate that can be read out of README section 1, Portal 10 and SF-01 (Schur complement exists, Haynsworth inertia additivity, congruence to diag(A, S), determinant and quotient identities, Loewner monotonicity) is a theorem for any block system with an invertible pivot, so the stated criterion does not separate the listed rows from unrelated systems.
scope: Two panels of 360 systems (seeds 20261121, 11235813; sizes 2 to 12) and a third independent panel of 576 (sizes 2 to 10), over Q and Q(i). Every test passes wherever its hypothesis holds. Partition scrambling leaves the pass count of every theorem test unchanged. The pseudo-inverse form exists for every matrix. Inertia additivity with it is guaranteed when the range condition A A^+ B = B holds (the matrix is then congruent to diag(A, S)), so the condition is sufficient. It is not necessary. Exact witnesses with symmetric M = [[A,B],[B^T,D]]: (1) A = [[-1,-1],[-1,-1]], B = [-1,-1]^T, D = [-1]: the condition holds and In(M) = (0,1,2) = (0,1,1) + (0,0,1). (2) A = [0], B = [1], D = [0]: the condition fails and In(M) = (1,1,0) is not (0,0,2). (3) A = [0], B = [[1,0]], D = [[0,1],[1,0]]: the condition fails and the inertia still adds, (1,1,1) = (0,0,1) + (1,1,0). In exhaustive small searches (entries in {-1,0,1}) the condition held in 75 and 27 of 243 systems with additivity in every one, and failed in 168 and 216 with additivity in 0 and 32. It fails in 6 of 720 systems of the panels. The identities themselves are textbook theorems (exact argument); the pass counts are sampled.

statement: Row 4 is a (min,+) system with no additive inverse, so no additive Schur complement exists for that object itself. Its Q[q] lift has an exact elimination (G5-13, G5-18). Row 6 is a non-Hermitian Liouvillian: inertia is undefined, its coupling is antisymmetric (exactly +-2g at the 15 points with omega = 0) and its pivot is negative definite, so no minimum exists (17 of 17 points). The quadratic form of M does not see the coupling: the Schur complement of its symmetric part is the symmetric part of D, not S(M). Both rows lie outside the invariant as SF-01 states it.

statement: No equivalence exists among the three matrix rows tested (spectral inertia, the Liouvillian, AeST). Each pairing fails on size, symmetry type or inertia of the reduced block, or on a determinant class. No transformation in the seven families rescues the equivalence non-vacuously (Law 2b, G5-20).
scope: Equivalence over Q(i) by dimension, signature and determinant class (Landherr), partition respecting. Cross-domain pairs: 108 of 168 spectral inertia against AeST fail on reduced inertia, 59 on the pivot determinant class and 1 on the reduced determinant class. The one near-match holds only after a unit rescale chosen for that pair (1 of 168 real pairs against 12 of 1,401 random symmetric 3x3 pairs, sampled). Only one regime of R_opt is a Schur value (51 of the ledger's own 420 instances). Equivalence over Q by Hasse invariants was not tested. Law 2b recheck, square classes of rational determinants (a different class group from the Q(i) norm classes above, so the counts differ): 0 of 168 pairs agree. 108 fail on the inertia of the reduced block, 60 more on the square class of det A, and every one of the 168 fails on the square class of both det A and det S. A global shift M + 871 I makes all 38 row 1 and row 5 objects positive definite, so 168 of 168 pairs then agree in inertia, as would random pairs (vacuous). The value 871 is a bound for rows 1 and 5 only. The row 6 matrices have row sums up to about 5,003, and sym(M) + 871 I is positive definite at only 15 of its 17 points.

statement: If no diagonal D makes D L symmetric, S is zero. If such a D is unique up to scale and the stress is non-zero, S has rank 1. The converse fails (smallest witness diag(3,2,2)); the transformed statement that holds is the rank formula of G5-07 (family T6). A plain basis change of the same lattice loses the collapse in 44 of 45 small cases and 4 of 4 at n=8. A carried change, which keeps every bar vector, leaves S_el unchanged and gives S_lat' = (U^-1 x I)^T S_lat (U^-1 x I) (family T1, transformed-exact).
scope: n >= 3. The proviso that the intra-cell framework has only rigid motions is removed for every n >= 3: the flex classification in Theorem B's proof shows that for n >= 3 the only flexes are rigid motions, and at n = 2 an extra flex exists. Basis: exact tests on instances (second/out/c5_thmB.txt) plus a step-by-step reading of the proof by an independent reader. Not machine-checked. Both implications were also checked exactly by the second checker on 904 lattices (n=3..6 and n=8). Basis-change counts: 45 cases at n=3..5 and 4 at n=8. Law 2b recheck by two checkers at n = 3 and 4: naive change keeps the collapse in 0 of 16, carried change leaves S_el unchanged in 16 of 16; L = diag(3,2,2) has rank 1 with dim Z_B = 3.

statement: For n >= 3 and rational L (n is the size of L): on Z_B = {z : diag(z) L symmetric}, sigma(z) = diag(z) L (L - 2I), and rank S = dim Z_B - dim{z in Z_B : z_i = 0 wherever row i of L (L - 2I) is non-zero}. The formula is refuted at n = 2, with witnesses L = diag(3,2) (actual rank 0, formula 1) and L = 3I (actual rank 1, formula 2).
scope: n >= 3, rational L. Instances: 1,725 (900 at n = 3, 600 at n = 4, 180 at n = 5 and 45 at n = 6, across 15 families), 0 mismatches. Two constructions of S_el agree on 40 of 40. Must-fail controls caught: dropping the second term (677 of 1,725), formula + 1 (1,725), L - 2I in place of L (L - 2I) (486), min(dim Z_B, 1) (737). Step checks: dim ker of the intra-cell map is n + n(n-1)/2 for n = 3 to 6. 128 of 128 basis vectors of Z_B lift to self-stresses with virial diag(z) L (L - 2I). The statement 'lift exists iff z in Z_B' held on 60 of 60 random z. n = 2: the formula is wrong on 237 of 400 random instances, and the intra-cell map has one extra flex (dim ker 4, rigid motions 3). Instances were tested for n = 3 to 6. The proof reading covers all n >= 3. Singular L is allowed.

statement: Over Q[q] with val(K_BB) >= 1: val(S_ij) >= T_ij, with equality exactly when the leading-coefficient sum over the minimizing walks is non-zero. Where that sum is zero and S_ij is non-zero, 1 <= val(S_ij) - T_ij <= (|B|+1)D - T_ij, with D the largest degree of an entry.
scope: val(K_BB) >= 1 over Q[q]. Instances: 7,600 (n = 3 to 6, |B| = 1 to n-1, D = 1 to 4), 27,502 entries with T finite. Violations of the lower bound, of [q^T]S = L, and of the equality condition: 0 of 27,502. L = 0 and S non-zero on 1,416 entries: gap bound held on 1,416 of 1,416, attained on 21. Exhaustive family |A| = 2, |B| = 1 (177,147 systems): val(S) <= 2D attained in 520. Must-fail controls caught: val >= T+1 (25,632 entries), val <= T (1,870), sign-blind rule (1,870), gap bound one lower (268), lead = L+1 (27,502), single hop with no Kleene star (853). The team's sentence that the regularity condition is necessary is not adopted. Observed, not proved (sampled-exact evidence): in a random panel that allowed val(K_BB) = 0, the lower bound failed only where det(I - K_BB)(0) = 0 (1,377 violations in 3,733 entries) and never where it was non-zero (0 violations in 41,702 entries, with 260 systems skipped because det is identically 0). The output does not count how many of the 41,702 entries have val(K_BB) = 0. One hand-built system with val(K_BB) = 0 and det(I - K_BB) = -1 satisfies the bound, but there the set of minimizing walks is infinite.

statement: Under Law 2b, the claim that Sylvester inertia is additive for the row 6 Liouvillian (In(M) = In(A) + In(S) with M Hermitian) is invariant-falsified: all seven families were searched and the obstruction is the antisymmetric coupling C = -B^T with B non-zero.
scope: 17 sampled Liouvillian points. No diagonal or block-diagonal similarity over C, no congruence, no complex affine map c M + lambda I and no partition-respecting compression makes M Hermitian while keeping a coupling (trace argument, rank of M - M^*, and exhaustive enumeration of all 65,025 partition-respecting coordinate subsets, 20,225 of which are Hermitian and all decoupled). Tropicalization has no instance. A non-block-diagonal similarity to a real symmetric matrix exists at 10 of 17 points (diagonalizable with real spectrum) and carries no Schur complement with it. The one exact repair, spectral inertia (eigenvalues counted by the sign of the real part), holds at 17 of 17 points but is true of nearly any system of the same shape (G5-20). Other Liouvillian parameters were not tested.

scope: Domain: non-negative coefficients and val(K_BB) >= 1 (G5-10, G5-13). On the 32-state matrix K: 528 of 528 blocks of size 1 and 2. The inverse becomes a Kleene star; the inertia statement is not part of this claim. Cancellation witness, inside val(K_BB) >= 1 but outside non-negative coefficients: K_00 = -q^2, K_01 = K_10 = q, K_11 = 0 gives val(S_00) = infinity against a tropical value of 2. Witness outside val(K_BB) >= 1: K_22 = 1 - q, K_02 = K_21 = q gives val(S_01) = 1 against 2.

statement: Row 4 inertia clause under Law 2b: neither certificate applies. It is not invariant-falsified, because block-diagonal symmetrizations exist for some singleton blocks. scope: Shown at q = 1/10, 1/100 and 1/1000 for blocks of size 1 and 2 (528 partitions of the 32 states), by exact null spaces and exact positive-definiteness tests: no fully diagonal gauge works; for 480 of 528 partitions the solution space is {0}, so no block-diagonal P exists; for the 9 pairs that contain a one-way edge no P exists at any q (K_BB = [[0,k],[0,0]] forces a zero diagonal entry); for the 16 antipodal pairs the one-dimensional solution is indefinite; a positive definite solution exists for 8 of 32 singletons at q = 1/10 and 18 of 32 at q = 1/100 and 1/1000. An unrestricted P exists at those q (32 distinct real eigenvalues). At q = 1/2 no real P of any shape exists. Where P exists, I - K is positive definite, so every inertia is (size,0,0). Not decided: symbolic q, blocks of size 3 or more, P depending on q beyond these three values.
